title: Capacity Sprint KPI & Tradeoff Lab Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working lab note for the upcoming capacity sprint (Q2 pilot -> 3rd-month scale). Goal: produce a pragmatic, engineer-friendly set of KPIs, an explicit tradeoff matrix, and an actionable readiness checklist for a staged rollout where we intentionally trade latency headroom for cost efficiency in tiered traffic. Use this doc to surface unresolved constraints and owners.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Objective: 3x pilot throughput while keeping 95th p50 latency increase <= 30% and cost-per-1000-tokens <= $0.80.
- Primary constraints: GPU reservation lead time, cross-region failover complexity, KV cache hit-rate for common prefixes.
- Current hypothesis: we can reduce unit cost by 20% if prefix caching and batching policies are tuned per-route combined with a single-step canary that routes 20% traffic to a quantized variant.

Key KPIs (what we will measure during the sprint):
- Latency SLOs: p50, p95 (ms) per route; target p95 <= 500ms for interactive routes, <= 1500ms for async batch routes.
- Cost metrics: $ per 1k tokens (generation), $ per 1k embeddings. Include GPU-hours burned by model variant.
- Reliability: error rate (5xx) per 1000 requests, fallback rate (requests that used variant fallback).
- Quality guardrails: semantic-acceptance rate on synthetic prompt set (target >= 95% pass for pilot).
- Cache effectiveness: KV cache hit rate (percent of tokens skipped via cache) and median cache reuse window (s).
- Operational metrics: time-to-rotate-capacity (minutes), incident MTTR (minutes).

Tradeoff matrix (working):
Columns = change; Rows = impact (latency, cost, quality, ops risk) scored -2..+2, plus notes.
1) Aggressive batching + 2s batching window: latency -2, cost +2, quality 0, ops risk +1. Notes: good for batch workers, hurts interactive UX.
2) Quantized model variant (8-bit): latency +1, cost +2, quality -1, ops risk 0. Notes: requires regen tests; risk of small quality regressions on edge prompts.
3) KV prefix caching on routes with repeat prefixes: latency +1, cost +1, quality +0, ops risk +1. Notes: high upside for chatbots with repeated system prompts.
4) Regional sticky routing (route by region then fallback): latency +1, cost -1, quality 0, ops risk +2. Notes: reduces cross-region egress but complex for canaries.

Acceptance criteria for pilot -> scale decision (must be met to move from 20% canary to 50%):
- p95 latency increase for canary cohort <= 30% relative to baseline for interactive routes.
- Error rate delta (canary vs baseline) < 0.5% absolute.
- Semantic-acceptance on evaluation suite >= 95% and no high-severity prompt regressions (manual review).
- Operational runbook validated: failover time <= 5 minutes in rehearsal, autoscaling events < 3 during a 48h window (to avoid oscillation).

Readiness checklist (working, non-exhaustive):
[ ] Model variants tagged and immutable (git tag + artifact URI)
[ ] Canary traffic policy configured (20% sticky), abort threshold set in console
[ ] Monitoring dashboards: latency breakdown by token position, cache hit-rate, fallback counts
[ ] Post-deploy smoke test: 50 synthetic chat turns across 10 personas
[ ] SLO alert playbook updated with on-call owner and escalation path
[ ] Cost alert: projected burn > 30% of sprint budget triggers finance review
[ ] Backpressure policy: rate-limiter + queue fallback for sustained >2x baseline RPS
[ ] Runbook: explicit rollback steps and model pin for traffic split

Experiment plan and schedule (2-week sprint cadence):
- Week 1 (days 1–5): instrument metrics (cache, per-token latency), baseline capture, small scale bench (1 GPU pool), implement variant artifact.
- Week 1, end: gate review (ops + eng) to greenlight canary.
- Week 2 (days 6–10): 20% canary for 48h with synthetic + live traffic shadowing. Collect metrics and run evals.
- Week 2, days 11–12: quality manual pass + regression review. If sat, expand to 50% for 72h.
- Week 2, day 14: retro and go/no-go decision.

Operational run scenarios (priority order):
1) Canary quality regression detected -> immediate rollback to baseline model, page SRE owner, pause scaling policies.
2) p95 latency > threshold but error rate stable -> reduce batching window + increase worker count within Dedicated pool.
3) Cache thrash observed -> increase TTL on prefix entries and flag high-cardinality routes for manual review.
4) Region failure -> activate cross-region fallback routing and notify customer success for impacted customers.

Open questions & unresolved items (action owners):
- GPU reservation: how long to spin up extra Dedicated GPUs across zones? (Owner: Diego Alvarez)
- Finance cadence: should we pre-commit buffer for sprint to avoid mid-sprint throttles? (Owner: Rhea Patel)
- Eval coverage: do we have a prompt set that represents (i) short intents, (ii) long-context rewrites, and (iii) multi-turn persona handoffs? (Owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Metrics bucketization: confirm granularity for cost slices (per-route vs per-tenant) to inform billing. (Owner: Maya Chen)

Mini runbook snippets (for on-call):
- If canary error rate delta > 0.5%: abort traffic split, revert canary using console rollback (model-pin to baseline), run full synthetic suite, escalate to product-ops lead.
- If p95 spikes but error stable: check KV cache hit-rate and tail queue depth. If cache hit-rate < 20% and tail queue depth > 80%: temporarily disable batching on that route.

Notes to selves (informal):
- Try a micro-experiment: 10% traffic + 0.5s batching but with prioritized short-request lane; could preserve interactive latency while gaining batching wins.
- Consider building a per-tenant budget guard: block fallthrough to quantized variant if tenant flagged for strict quality SLA.

Appendix: quick reference numbers (bench):
- Baseline interactive p95: 380ms, p50: 110ms
- Baseline cost: $1.02 per 1k gen tokens
- Quantized variant bench (local): p95 420ms, cost projection $0.76 per 1k tokens
- Typical KV hit-rate on recent chat routes: 18% median (per past 30d)

Action items (next 7 days):
- Diego: confirm GPU warmup time across zones and post in thread (#prodops-capacity) by EOD Thu.
- Rhea: draft sprint budget buffer proposal and 2 alternatives (pre-commit vs burst credits) by Tue.
- Liam: finalize eval prompt set and add 100 edge prompts for manual review by Wed.
- Maya: add dashboard panels (cache hit-rate, per-route batching latency) and link to doc.

End of doc. This is intentionally terse and iterative; expect edits. Keep thread: #prodops-capacity.
